sentences.text: This appellant/Insurance Company has come forward with this appeal seeking quantum of compensation in the judgment and decree dated 22.12.2014 in MACTOP. No.29/2002 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Arni.
2. It is the case of the appellant that on 10.12.2001 at about 09.05 am.
The first respondent and her son were going in their motor cycle, at that time, the second respondent driven the bus in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle.
Due to the accident, the first respondent and her son sustained grievous injuries and admitted in Government Hospital.

Thereafter, the first respondent herein, has filed a Claim Petition before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Arni,
claiming Rs.1,00,000/- as compensation under various heads.
3. Denying the allegations of the claimant, the appellant insurance company filed a counter affidavit before the Tribunal.
During the trial before the Tribunal, on the side of the claimant, two witnesses were https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis examined and and marked four documents viz., Exs.P1 to P4.
On the side of the respondents, one witness was examined and five documents were marked.
4. The Tribunal, considering the oral and documentary evidence, allowed the petition in part and awarded a sum of Rs.30,000/- as compensation to the claimant.
Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation, the appellant insurance company has filed this appeal before this Court.

5. The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the vehicle involved in the said accident was insured with the third respondent, not insured with the appellant and the first respondent has not been produced a copy of the insurance policy of the vehicle.
Therefore, the appellant is not liable to pay the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
On the sole ground, the appeal is liable to be set aside.

6. The learned counsel for the third respondent submitted that the first respondent's son has filed another appeal before this Court in CMA No.3397 of 2008, the appellant has pleaded the very same point before this https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Court and the same was dismissed vide order dated 06.08.2019.

7. Heard both sides and perused the materials available on record.
8.

Upon perusal of the award passed by the Tribunal it is evident that the Tribunal has taken note of the contents of the FIR with the evidence of PW1 and has fixed the liability on the appellant herein.

Eventhough it is argued on the side of the appellant that vehicle involved in the accident was not insured with them and the claimant has not produced the copy of the insurance policy, neither oral not documentary evidence has been placed by the appellant to substantiate the said contention.
Hence, the negligence fixed by the Tribunal on the appellant cannot be faulted, since the same is based on evidence and documents produced with no contra evidence on record.
Hence, the award does not require any interference by this Court.
The amount awarded to the claimant is reasonable and hence the same are also confirmed.

sentences.text: In view of the above, this Court do not find any error in the award passed by the Tribunal.

There is no merit in the appeal and therefore, this https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Court is not inclined to interfere with the same.
10.
In the result, the Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is dismissed.

The appellant insurance company is directed to deposit the entire amount awarded by the Tribunal along with interest at 7.5%, less the amount already deposited if any, within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.

On such deposit being made, the first respondent/claimant, is permitted to withdraw the compensation as awarded by the Tribunal along with interest and costs, less the amount, if any,
already withdrawn, by filing an appropriate application before the Court concerned.
No costs.
